title: BROOD DataOps extraction contract
provenance: second pass. i looped over every tab in all four june files with tools/inspect_workbook.py instead of the first few. that found 2 more branches and most of the ignore_columns.

conventions.text_normalisation: trim, collapse spaces inside, uppercase. that is all. no spelling fixes apart from the aliases listed below. G YEAR and FZONE stay as typed because I do not know the real names.
conventions.blank_cell_semantics: a blank qty cell means not recorded. it is not 0 and it is not data. a tab where every product row is blank still counts as a tab, it loads 0 rows and the gap goes in the report.
conventions.numeric_rule: excel numbers as they are, rounded to 6 dp to drop float dust. text cells: strip spaces, digits only, or one comma with exactly 3 digits after it which is a thousands separator. anything else becomes non_numeric_qty.
conventions.date_rule: day tabs have no date cells. the day comes from the tab name, the month and year from this contract. sales tabs carry dd.mm.yyyy dates. both end up as YYYY-MM-DD. the sales files say 2023 and the june files say 2026, I keep what each file states.
conventions.dup_policy_day_grid: for a (date, product, branch) key the first row wins, later ones go to quarantine as duplicate_key.
conventions.ignore_columns: columns in ignore_columns are not facts: the row totals, the prices and the money values. i drop them by contract. every tab that had something in one of them gets a note so the drop is visible.
conventions.aggregate_rows: each tab ends with a row whose item says TOTAL. that row is not a product and never loads as one. if a value was typed into its branch cells I quarantine it as aggregate_row_value.
conventions.row_total_column: when a source gives me the sheet's own TOTAL or TOTAL QUANTITY column I compare it to the sum of the branch cells I parsed from that row. rows that disagree become an anomaly note. I still load the row, the sheet's total is a hint not a gate.
conventions.unnamed_columns: a column with no header text but with values under it. I cannot name it so I will not load it. the report tells me how many values were sitting in it.
conventions.branch_aliases: when a branch header is typed wrong but clearly sits in the branch spot I map it with an alias and add a note every time the alias is used.

ignore_columns.TOTAL: sum of the branch cells on that row, not a 15th branch
ignore_columns.UNIT: unit price, only on the 1st tab
ignore_columns.PRICE: unit price, typed on some tabs
ignore_columns.TOTAL COST: money column, the arithmetic in the file does not add up
ignore_columns.VALUE: money column on the 1OTH JUNE tab

ignore_sheets.SUMMARY: month summary in RWF, not units. cannot be lined up with the day tabs so the contract drops it

notes: 26 tabs here. 25 are day tabs and they cover the 1st to the 25th. there is no tab at all for the 26th to the 30th, so expected_days says 1-30 and the report shows that 5 days are simply not in the file. i am not going to invent them.
the 19th to the 25th tabs each have exactly one product row recorded. i checked this rather than trusting the first look, which had told me those tabs were empty.
the tab named 1OTH JUNE has the letter O where the 0 should be. fix_letter_O reads it as day 10, and there is no other 10th tab, so nothing collides.
late month tabs carry PRICE / TOTAL COST / VALUE. they are in ignore_columns so they stay out of the facts and are still visible in the report.

ignore_columns.TOTAL: sum of the branch cells on that row
ignore_columns.PRICE: unit price, typed on most tabs
ignore_columns.ITEM: the second ITEM header belongs to the side variance table, not to this grid
ignore_columns.VALUE: variance table, shows up twice so it is ignored twice
ignore_columns.DISPACH: variance table, the clerk spelled dispatch without the T
ignore_columns.CLOSING: stock side column on the 1st and 14th tabs

ignore_sheets.PRODUCTION VARIANCE: aggregate variance sheet, not a day tab
ignore_sheets.PRODUCTION: half filled month sheet, not a day tab
ignore_sheets.TEST: not a data tab, that is what it is called
ignore_sheets.DISPATCH VS PRODUCTION: comparison sheet, not a day tab

notes: some day tabs put a number in column A above the header, the 22nd one does. the header search walks down until it finds ITEM, and column A is always the row number.
most tabs have a variance and stock table sitting to the right of the branch grid. its columns are all in ignore_columns.
the 1OTH JUNE letter O tab is read as day 10, same as production.
one value was typed inside the TOTAL row of the 22nd tab. aggregate_rows puts it in quarantine.

ignore_columns.TOTAL QUANTITY: sum of the branch cells on that row
ignore_columns.TOTAL: money value at the bottom right
ignore_columns.AMOUNT: unit price metadata, typed on some tabs
ignore_columns.PRICE: unit price as above, on the 23rd tab

ignore_sheets.SUMARY: aggregate tab, note the missing M in the name

notes: waste is sparse, usually single units per branch. blank cells stay not recorded.

on the 14th tab the G YEAR header is typed GDYEAR. it sits exactly where G YEAR sits on the other tabs, that tab has no separate G YEAR column and it holds real numbers, so branch_aliases maps it to G YEAR. every use shows up as a note.
the tabs do not all carry the same extra columns. TOTAL QUANTITY is on most of them, AMOUNT and PRICE only sometimes, so ignore_columns is the union of what I saw.

ignore_columns.TOTAL: sum of the branch cells, and every value in it is a typed 0 next to blank branch cells

notes: every product row on all 6 tabs was blank when I wrote this contract. each row has a typed 0 in its TOTAL cell. so this source loads 0 rows and the report shows the gap. I keep the source in the run on purpose, dropping it would hide a real problem with the data.
the double space in the file name is part of the real name so I keep it in the path.

whether the empty first six days of returns means nothing came back or it is recorded elsewhere.
KITCHEN is an item row on every tab. if it ever carries numbers i am not sure what it is.
